subject.title: Feature request: Hook event for context pruning

question: Should OpenClaw expose a pruning lifecycle hook now, and should the contract be metadata-only by default rather than exposing raw pruned content?
rationale: The implementation direction is clear enough, but the payload and delivery semantics affect session privacy, installed hook trust, and agent availability.

options.title: Metadata-only session:prune
options.body: Expose a bounded event from the active pruning path with counts, timing, and sanitized optional tool identifiers, while keeping raw pruned content out of the default payload.

options.title: Raw-content opt-in design
options.body: Allow richer pruned-content access only behind an explicit security-reviewed opt-in contract with size, timeout, and logging guidance.

options.title: Defer the hook
options.body: Keep scheduled indexing or memory plugins as the supported workaround until maintainers are ready to define a pruning hook boundary.

recommendation.title: Metadata-only session:prune
recommendation.body: Expose a bounded event from the active pruning path with counts, timing, and sanitized optional tool identifiers, while keeping raw pruned content out of the default payload.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest routing owner from cache-TTL pruning history, active-path refactors, and prior maintainer review on this issue.
